blocks.text: Isaiah speaks through many voices, including divine speech, communal voices, heralds, servants, personified cities, and third-person narration. Speaker identity therefore needs to be established passage by passage; in Isaiah 63, the answering figure of verses 1–6 gives way to a communal remembrance and appeal beginning in verse 7. The book’s transmission also has a substantial ancient witness: the nearly complete Great Isaiah Scroll broadly agrees with the Masoretic tradition while containing numerous spelling and substantive differences, and other Qumran Isaiah manuscripts show continued transmission and interpretation.
